turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because... well, I drive a taxi, and I always do my safety checks before I start my shift. But lately, even when I know I did the check, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something on the cab. I start thinking somebody could get hurt, or my boss is gonna think I lied about doing the check. It's just... I can't make it shut up while I'm driving, or even when I'm trying to study. It's really getting in the way.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes persistent, intrusive, and unwanted thoughts of having missed a vehicle safety check and causing harm, which they cannot suppress, characteristic of obsessions.

turns.doctor_question: When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly — like checking things again, counting, or going through a specific routine — to try to ease the worry?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Before I can even take a ride, I just keep going around the car. I'll check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, and all my paperwork... just over and over again. 

Sometimes I even take pictures of everything with my phone, and, well, if the check doesn't feel exactly right, I have to restart the whole routine from the beginning. It's really frustrating because I'll be out there doing this even when passengers are standing right there waiting for me and I'm already late. I just can't stop myself until it feels done.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive, rigid checking rituals (tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork, taking photos) that must be restarted if they do not feel right, performed compulsively despite causing delays and distress.

turns.doctor_question: How do you feel if you're not able to complete your checking routine the way you want to?
turns.patient_response:
Honestly, it feels terrible. If a passenger rushes me and I have to drive off before it feels right... I just get really, really panicked. 

My brain just keeps screaming at me that the car isn't safe and someone is going to get hurt, and it'll be all my fault. I can't even focus on the road or listen to what the customer is saying. It's just this huge, overwhelming sense of dread. I basically can't function or think straight until I can find an excuse to pull over somewhere and finish the routine.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes intrusive, distressing obsessional thoughts that the car is unsafe, someone will get hurt, and it will be their fault.
symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient reports being compelled to pull over and finish their checking routine to alleviate overwhelming dread and panic.

turns.doctor_question: When you do your checks, is it to make sure that nothing bad happens, like someone getting hurt or your boss thinking you lied?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, exactly. That's the whole reason. Like I was saying before, that's why I keep going around the car checking the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, and my paperwork over and over. I just have to be absolutely sure nothing bad is gonna happen. 

That's why I take the pictures and why I have to restart the whole check if it doesn't feel right... I'm just trying to prevent someone from getting hurt or my boss thinking I'm lying. It's why I keep doing it even when I'm already late and the passengers are just standing there waiting for me. I just have to know it's safe.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive checking rituals, taking pictures, and restarting checks to prevent feared catastrophic outcomes such as someone getting hurt or being accused of lying.
